narrative:
The model determined that you have about a 30% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the loan amount you requested, and your installment rate as a percentage of disposable income. Your checking account status was the single biggest reason for the denial. Having a negative balance (<0 DM) is relatively uncommon among approved applicants (only 12.6% of them show this status), and it pushed the prediction noticeably toward higher risk. In contrast, the amount you asked for (2,462 DM) was lower than the average requested by approved borrowers (about 3,020 DM). This lower amount actually worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward approval. Similarly, your installment rate of 2% of disposable income is better than the 3% average seen among those who were approved, which also helped reduce the risk score.

Even though two of the top factors spoke in your favor, the negative signal from your checking account proved decisive. To improve your chances on a future application, focus first on bringing your checking account balance into positive territory and maintaining it there for several months. This single change would likely have the largest positive impact on how a similar model would evaluate you next time.
